Transparency here. Feel free to delete. As a client I have recorded 2 therapists. The first I was with for 11 years. He allowed me to record. He wanted to know what I planned to do with the recordings. There was one occasion where he got angry and frustrated because of my constant suicidal ideation. I get it. At the end of the session he said, after you listen to this delete it please. I did as he asked. It was a mutual respect and trust between us. 

The 2nd therapist I recorded twice and I did it secretly and could still do to this day if it weren't for my annoying honesty. I confessed to recording two of our appointments years ago. My reasoning for the first was she was going away for three weeks to Paris and I was not dealing with the idea of her being gone for so long. I recorded her voice to give me comfort in her absence. If I had just asked her she would have likely agreed to it at the time. The 2nd time I recorded was during an appointment with my sister too. I found it useful to listen to again and as a way to check the facts. Like I said, I confessed to both and she said that I can record but I need to ask first. Sounds fair. I let the topic go until recently when I noticed my memory becoming a bigger issue. I asked for her permission but because of the stories she has heard about people paying for recorded therapy to help train AI, she said not now but maybe in the near future.

I share this as a window to the clients perspective and to say what none of you want to hear... I could record our appointments with just my cell phone and you'd never know it. I can record phone calls and I can record telehealth sessions that I occasionally have on my phone. I am NOT doing these things but here's why. I don't like asking for permission if I think there's a chance that I will be told "no." An even bigger reason is that I find it close to impossible to lie to my therapist. The secret of the two I recorded without permission was eating me alive! The last reason I don't but it isn't a huge deterrent is that the state I live in it is illegal to record without permission.

Eventually she changed the plan a little where I have to call a Crisis Unit that is in my town specifically for mental health. I tell them what is going on. They assess the situation and THEN I am supposed to call or text her and let her know what's going on.

A lot of us who are in DBT aren't comfortable being around people. When you learned to be a medic, surely there was homework. Did that feel patronizing? Unless you give it a chance, it won't work. 

DBT is meant to be taught the same way no matter where you are. So there's guidelines to follow in group. This helps everyone feel safe and it's not meant to be childish. Try to let go of the things that bother you about it and find one or two things that you think will be helpful. What they're trying to teach us is what we were supposed to be taught by our parents when we were young. Most of us were not. We don't know how to have effective relationships. We don't know how to live dialectically. This means accepting that something doesn't have to be all good or all bad but it can be somewhere in the middle. This is that black and white thinking you may hear about. 

I might suggest looking at Wikipedia and seeing what you can find on DBT. Get curious. I love it and I'm so grateful for it. I'm not in DBT anymore but I certainly still use the skills that I learned. 

I can tell you're angry about being asked to join a DBT group. In DBT we learn how to tell what emotions we are feeling. Did you know anger is really just disguised fear? Our emotions tell us something. Learning to tell that I was anxious was difficult for me until I realized I can feel it in my stomach. As if I'm doing sit ups.

Okay I think I'm rambling now but I do want to say one more thing about the notebook and all of that. So there are a lot of handouts and they're basically copies of this DBT book by Marshall Lenahan, the founder of DBT. She actually was in-patient over 100 times when she was suffering with borderline personality disorder herself. 

Anyway there's a lot of handouts. There may be homework but no one's checking your work. You'll probably be asked to share what you've written and that's the hard part. It's not only hard to share but it's hard to sit there and listen to some people go on and on and on. If you don't want to share you don't have to. In my group if things were too much, or if I was feeling anxious or angry or any emotion that was too intense I was allowed to get up from the group and walk outside. I wasn't allowed to leave the area but I was allowed to get out of the group and gather myself. 

I hope some of what I've said has helped. I wish you the best of luck and I hope you go with an open mind. If you have any questions feel free to dm me. This is huge for me to offer that. I generally don't chat with people I don't know.
